b: The Salesforce FIDE World Championship 2026 will be a match to remember. While the players are bringing novelties to the chessboard, the official broadcast on the FIDE YouTube channel is introducing innovations of its own. Viewers can follow every move with world-class commentary, exclusive interviews, AI-powered insights and live reports directly from the playing venue.

The broadcast team brings together some of the most recognizable names in chess. Leading the analysis are grandmasters Peter Svidler and Peter Leko. Svidler is an eight-time Russian Champion and one of the most respected commentators in the chess world, combining elite-level expertise with an engaging style. Leko, a former World Championship challenger, came within half a point of becoming World Champion in his 2004 title match against Vladimir Kramnik. Together, they explain the players' plans and calculations in a way that is accessible to all chess fans.

Grandmaster Maurice Ashley, a fan favourite, serves as host and presenter. He introduces the players before the start of each game, guides viewers through the day's action, and regularly joins Svidler and Leko in the studio discussion.

Meanwhile, charming Charlize van Zyl reports directly from the venue, bringing viewers closer to the championship atmosphere through interviews, behind-the-scenes content, and live updates from the fan zone.

Those who missed the opening day should make time to watch the hour-long pre-game show. All four hosts spent an hour discussing the players' chances, preparation teams, psychological factors, opening expectations, and many of the storylines that could shape the match. Even before the first move was played, it offered valuable insights into what may ultimately decide the world title.

It is 2026, and chess broadcasting is evolving with the times. This year's production introduces several new features that give viewers unique analytical tools and deeper insights into the games. They were developed by none other than Indian Grandmaster Vidit Gujrathi, renowned as a top player, popular streamer, and now, AI developer.
Chief Executive Adviser of the FIDE President, Emil Sutovsky explained the vision behind the new setup:
This production represents the first step in an ambitious project - where we aim to transform the fan experience. We gathered a very capable team, which produced a result within short period of time.

GM Vidit Gujrathi played a central role in shaping the concept, and together we have laid the foundation for what we see as the future of chess coverage. We will continue developing it over the coming months to deliver the final product in Q2 2027.

Among the most exciting innovations is the FIDE Predictor. Rather than simply calculating the strongest engine move, the Predictor analyses vast numbers of games to estimate which move a human grandmaster is most likely to play in a given position. The prediction is not necessarily the objectively best move. Instead, it attempts to capture human decision-making. As the game unfolds, viewers can compare the prediction with what actually happened on the board, creating a unique opportunity to evaluate both the players and the Predictor itself.
GM Vidit Gujrathi shared his perspective on the new tool:

I thought that simply reading out Stockfish moves doesn't really provide insight into human thinking. So, a while ago, I started developing the Predictor as a fun project. More broadly, I've always had the philosophy that we should make chess more exciting and engaging to reach more people. Emil reached out to me, and we quickly realized that we shared the same vision. We started working, but at first we assumed we wouldn't have enough time to implement it for the World Championship, so we were mainly thinking about future events. But the initial prototype looked good, and we decided to take a chance and use it already in Geneva. It was definitely a risk, but I'm really happy with how the first day went and that a lot of people found it exciting.

The broadcast also provides a wealth of statistical information throughout the game. During Game 1, for example, viewers could immediately see that Gukesh had already spent significantly more time than his opponent in the opening phase, falling 18 minutes behind on the clock after only twelve moves. The "Time Spent" graphic is just one example of the data available.

The last five moves are displayed together with their evaluations, allowing viewers to follow the evolution of the position at a glance. According to the engine, the first game featured remarkably accurate play, with no major mistakes from either side.

Another feature tracks the players' winning chances throughout the game. With every move, the agent recalculates the probabilities and updates its assessment. On move 13 of Game 1, the draw probability stood at 62%, with Sindarov given a 21% chance of winning and Gukesh 17%. By move 20, the draw chances had dipped slightly to 59%, while Sindarov's winning chances increased to 30%.

The commentators were sceptical of such a large gap in Sindarov's favour from a human perspective, and the agent soon adjusted its assessment. Just one move later, the draw probability returned to 64%, with Sindarov's chances back at 21% and Gukesh's at 15%. Such fluctuations provide an additional layer of discussion and entertainment.

As fans have come to expect from major FIDE events, the live production combines multiple camera feeds from the playing hall with close-up shots of the players and the board, alongside a digital board displaying the position with complete clarity.
The commentators demonstrate possible variations, helping viewers understand not only what happened in the game but also the ideas and calculations that remained behind the scenes.

The broadcast also features distinguished guests. On the opening day, Viswanathan Anand, former World Champion and one of the greatest players in chess history, joined the studio. As always, Anand brought valuable insights drawn from his own World Championship experience, adding another dimension to the analysis.

Whether you are a dedicated chess fan or following the World Championship for the first time, the FIDE Channel offers far more than a simple live board. With elite commentary, exclusive venue access, special guests and cutting-edge AI features, it is the best way to experience every moment of the Salesforce FIDE World Championship Match from the comfort of your own screen.
